newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - German institutes raise 1996 GDP forecast.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - German institutes raise 1996 GDP forecast.

text.p: Germany's six leading research institutes raised to 1.5 percent their forecast for 1996 economic growth, from a projection of 0.75 percent growth they made in spring, coalition sources said on Monday.
The move is in line with upward revisions by private sector economists and a recent government statement that growth picked up in the third quarter from the previous quarter.
The institutes are due to release their semi-annual economic report on Tuesday.

Sluggish economic growth at the start of the year and continued high unemployment have swelled Germany's budget deficit, as Finance Minister Theo Waigel strains to pull state finances together to qualify for the single European currency.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats and their Free Democrat partners fought openly in the past two weeks over the best way to bridge the deficit, a row that threatened to scupper the coalition.

In the second quarter, the latest for which official figures are available, Germany's gross domestic product (GDP) increased 1.2 percent from the year-earlier quarter, after a pronounced slowdown late in 1995 and at the start of this year.
The institutes revised their forecast for 1996 west German GDP growth up to 1.5 percent from 0.5 percent, and for east German growth down to 2.0 percent from 3.0 percent, the sources said.
The six institutes expect economic growth in 1997 to rise to 2.5 percent, unchanged from the spring report. Inflation should remain subdued at 1.5 percent.
In the report, the number of jobless in Germany is seen rising to an average 4.0 million in 1997 from 3.95 million this year, the sources said.
